entities.text: Gottam Jyothi vs The State Of Telangana
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The Honourable Smt. Justice K. Sujana
 Criminal Petition No.9375 of 2024
Order:

This Criminal Petition is filed under Section 528 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (for short 'BNSS') by the petitioner seeking to quash the proceedings against her in Crime No.1119 of 2023 on the file of Cyber Crime Police Station, Cyberabad, registered for the alleged offences punishable under Section 420 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 and Section 66-D of the Information Technology Act, 2000-2008.

2. Heard Sri Seshagiri Rao Yalamanchili, learned counsel for the petitioner and Sri Arun Kumar Doddla, learned Additional Public Prosecutor for respondent No.1 - State.
3.

Without going into the merits of the case, since the punishment prescribed for the offences alleged against the petitioner is less than seven (07) years, this Court deems it appropriate to direct the petitioner to appear before the Investigating Officer on or before 28.08.2024 between 11:00 a.m.
and 05:00 p.m. and in turn, the Investigating Officer is directed to follow the procedure laid down under section 41-A of Criminal Procedure Code (presently Section 35(3) of the BNSS) and also the guidelines formulated by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in Arnesh Kumar v. State of Bihar 1 scrupulously.

entities.text: Arnesh Kumar v. State of Bihar 1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: However, the petitioner shall submit her defense and co-operate with the Investigating Officer as and when required by furnishing information and produce all relevant documents/material required for the purpose of the investigation and the Investigating Officer shall consider the same before filing appropriate report before the learned Magistrate concerned.
4. Accordingly, the Criminal Petition is disposed of.
Miscellaneous applications, if any pending, shall also stand closed.

Note:
Issue CC forthwith.
